chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a person in ihram who covered his head unintentionally. He said: 'He removes the head-covering from his head and says the Talbiyah, and there is no penalty upon him.'

key_terms.الْقِنَاعَ: The head-covering (specifically a cap or cloth that does not cover the face)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.وَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: And there is no penalty upon him
key_terms.وَيُلَبِّي: And he says the Talbiyah (the declaration of pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person in ihram covers their head by mistake?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that unintentional head covering (*nasiyan*) for men in ihram incurs no expiation (*damm*), distinguishing it from deliberate acts. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that minor violations due to forgetfulness do not break the sanctity of the pilgrimage state, allowing the pilgrim to simply remove the covering and resume the *Talbiyah*. It highlights the ease (*yusr*) in ritual law when the cause is lack of intent rather than negligence.
